extraction.name: POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation)
extraction.description: A dataset/benchmark for evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). POPE formulates hallucination evaluation as a binary classification task by prompting LVLMs with Yes-or-No questions about probing objects (e.g., 'Is there a car in the image?'). It includes three sampling strategies (Random, Popular, Adversarial) for constructing questions about nonexistent objects, built on top of MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA datasets.
extraction.creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen
extraction.publisher: Renmin University of China; Meituan Group
extraction.citeAs: Li, Y., Du, Y., Zhou, K., Wang, J., Zhao, W. X., & Wen, J.-R. (2023). Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models. arXiv:2305.10355v3.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors randomly selected 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects from the validation set of MSCOCO, and constructed 6 questions for each image. For A-OKVQA and GQA, images were annotated using the SEEM automatic segmentation tool. Questions were built using ground-truth objects (for 'Yes' answers) and sampled nonexistent objects (for 'No' answers) under three sampling strategies: Random, Popular, and Adversarial.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Source images and annotations from MSCOCO (validation set), A-OKVQA, and GQA datasets. For unannotated datasets, objects were extracted using SEEM (Segment Everything Everywhere all at once) automatic segmentation tool.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Questions are formulated using a template 'Is there a/an <object> in the image?'. The ratio between ground-truth and nonexistent objects is set to 1:1 for label balance. Three sampling strategies were used for nonexistent objects: Random (random sampling), Popular (top-k most frequent objects not in image), and Adversarial (top-k co-occurring objects not in image).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: 500 images were randomly selected from the MSCOCO validation set that contained more than 3 ground-truth objects. For each image, 6 questions were constructed (l=6). Objects were obtained either from human annotations or from SEEM segmentation tool outputs.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Ground-truth objects were obtained from existing human annotations of MSCOCO, or generated automatically using SEEM segmentation tool for A-OKVQA and GQA. Questions with 'Yes' answers were built using ground-truth objects, while 'No' questions were built by sampling from nonexistent objects using three different strategies.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Consistency analysis was conducted to measure whether Yes/No responses in POPE genuinely reflect models' perception of objects. Out of 1303 and 1445 objects given 'No' responses by InstructBLIP and MiniGPT-4, only 0 and 5 were referenced in captions, validating the reliability of POPE.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEEM (Segment Everything Everywhere all at once) for automatic segmentation; ChatGPT for VQA answer matching evaluation
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Object hallucination hinders safe use of LVLMs in real-world deployment. For example, autonomous driving systems making wrong decisions due to incorrect understanding of the external environment could lead to serious safety issues. The work aims to provide reliable hallucination evaluation to help develop more trustworthy LVLMs.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The visual instruction datasets of LVLMs are mostly constructed based on MSCOCO, sharing a similar unbalanced object distribution where top frequent objects occupy a major part. LVLMs are prone to hallucinate frequently appearing objects and frequently co-occurring objects in the visual instruction datasets.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The work only focuses on object hallucination, not other aspects of LVLM capabilities. Evaluation is done on a subset (500 images) of validation sets due to computational limitations. POPE uses matching-based methods for Yes/No determination, which may fail when LVLMs don't explicitly use these words. When combined with automatic segmentation, object granularity may differ from human annotations. Only a small number of LVLMs were evaluated, excluding some recent or closed-source models. The benchmark focuses on coarse-grained object hallucinations, leaving fine-grained aspects (number, attributes, positions) for future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing/Evaluation - POPE is designed for evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). It provides stable, fair, and flexible evaluation through binary classification tasks using Yes-or-No questions about probing objects.
